Chemokine.description:
Chemokine measurement (e.g., CXCL1, CXCL8/IL-8, CCL2, CCL20).
Chemokines orchestrate leukocyte recruitment to inflamed intestinal mucosa; elevated
levels correlate with neutrophil and monocyte infiltration and are increasingly used
as mechanistic biomarkers in IBD clinical trial endpoints.

Granulocyte.description:
Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor measurement (G-CSF, GM-CSF).
G-CSF and GM-CSF regulate neutrophil and macrophage production and activation;
GM-CSF deficiency has been implicated in impaired mucosal defense in Crohn's disease,
and sargramostim (GM-CSF) has been evaluated as a therapeutic in refractory CD.

Interferon.description:
Interferon cytokine measurement (e.g., IFN-γ, IFN-α).
IFN-γ is a key Th1 effector cytokine elevated in Crohn's disease mucosa and implicated
in granuloma formation; elevated IFN-γ in VEOIBD may signal an underlying monogenic
immune dysregulation such as IL-10 signaling defects.

Interleukin.description:
Interleukin cytokine measurement (e.g., IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12, IL-17, IL-23).
Interleukins are central mediators of mucosal inflammation in IBD; IL-6 and IL-8 correlate
with disease activity, IL-10 is anti-inflammatory, and IL-12/IL-23 drive the Th1/Th17
pathways targeted by ustekinumab and risankizumab.

TNF.description:
Tumor necrosis factor measurement (TNF-α).
TNF-α is a pleiotropic pro-inflammatory cytokine central to IBD pathogenesis and the
primary target of anti-TNF biologics (infliximab, adalimumab); serum levels may guide
therapeutic drug monitoring interpretation in refractory disease.

description:
IBD-relevant cytokine laboratory measurements.
Captures serum, plasma, or mucosal cytokine values used to characterize the
inflammatory milieu, stratify disease phenotype, and support mechanistic
research in pediatric IBD including VEOIBD immune dysregulation workup.

* interleukin: Pro- and anti-inflammatory interleukins (IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12, IL-17, IL-23).
* interferon: Interferon effector cytokines (IFN-γ, IFN-α); elevated in Th1-driven and monogenic IBD.
* tnf: Tumor necrosis factor alpha; primary anti-TNF biologic target.
* chemokine: Leukocyte recruitment mediators (CXCL8, CCL2, CCL20); correlate with mucosal infiltration.
* granulocyte: Colony-stimulating factors (G-CSF, GM-CSF); regulators of innate immune cell production.
title: IbdCytokineLabAnnotation
